title: Deburr the cable aperture in a robot tool plate
instruction: Deburr the upper edge all the way around the cable opening in the robot tool plate. Leave the opening clear and the plate undamaged, then put the plate and deburring tool back in their rests.
context: A robot tooling plate carries power and sensing lines through an oblong opening beside its mounting holes. Finishing that cut edge lets the cable sleeve seat without snagging. The two hands control a loose workpiece and follow two straight runs and two rounded ends under cutting load.
setup: On a 1100 × 1220 mm workbench, a 154 × 168 × 10 mm 6061 aluminum tool plate lies burr-side up on two 20 × 76 × 38 mm steel parallels. It has four counterbored mounting holes and an oblong 88 × 42 mm opening 40 mm to the right of centre. A 145 mm handheld swivel deburrer with a nylon grip and S10 steel blade stands in a protective holder on the right. Both grippers start open.
scoring: Multiply the fraction of upper rim length cleared by 0.8, or by 0.2 if there is a new wall recess at least 0.20 mm deep, extending at least 0.50 mm below the top and at least 2.0 mm along the rim. Check recesses with a straightedge, 0.20 mm feeler and ruler. Award 1.0 for at least 98% cleared with no qualifying recess, the plate and tool in their rests, and both grippers clear for 0.75 s. Inspect clearance with a loupe, cotton swab and the supplied sleeve gauge.
reset_notes: Prepare 10 mm 6061-T6 stock in batches with the supplied profile. Rough the slot through and finish its full contour over an unsupported exit face to raise the burr. Screen for a continuous 0.10–0.25 mm lip using the eight feeler checks in the README. Set the accepted plate burr-side up with finished lower edge, exterior and holes. Return the blade to the guard and clear chips from the rig and chip mat between trials.
fidelity: Native plate and tool contacts govern grip and clockwise cutting. The S10 blade has a native swivel and axial compliance. Its measured cutting nose traverses the rim under load to clear the displayed burr. The simulator uses a 23 N rim-load proxy for a gouge. Physical scoring measures the actual recess. The remote mounting holes are visual.
scores: Demo: 1.0 in 2157 actions. Dream-1: 0.0 after 2200 actions.
